description: Frankfurt has three near-parallel east-west runways -- 07C/25C (4,000 m), 07R/25L (4,000 m) and 07L/25R (2,800 m, genuinely shorter, confirmed by SkyVector's own length field, not a data error) -- plus 18 (4,000 m, north-south; the reciprocal end 36 is never used per VATGER, so omitted rather than listed dead). Headings are TRUE, not magnetic: ICAO Annex 3/WMO convention (and secondhand DWD citations) say METAR wind is coded true, so runway heading must match the wind-report frame (docs/NEW_AIRPORT_QUESTIONS.md section 2), same resolution as LSZH (docs/LSZH_RUNWAY_RESEARCH.md section 1). SkyVector's magnetic headings (068/248 trio, 178 for 18) were cross-checked against PilotNav's true set (069/249, 179); the ~1 degree gap matches Frankfurt's small magnetic variation. See docs/EDDF_RUNWAY_RESEARCH.md for full detail; not checked against the DFS eAIP.
source: SkyVector and PilotNav EDDF pages, cross-checked against each other, 31-10-2026. Thresholds: SkyVector's decimal-minute coordinates; 18's threshold cross-checked against PilotNav (matched to within 30 m). Not checked against the DFS eAIP. See docs/EDDF_RUNWAY_RESEARCH.md.
